items.text: Rescued chimpanzees from research laboratories are receiving specialized lifelong care at the Second Chance Chimpanzee Refuge in Liberia. Many of these animals were originally captured from the wild as infants and spent years inside testing facilities. Today, they live in social groups on mangrove-covered islands where they can roam freely. Because these West African chimpanzees belong to a subspecies listed as critically endangered on the IUCN Red List due to rapidly declining numbers, protecting them is essential. To monitor their health as they age, specialists conduct comprehensive medical examinations, including blood tests, fecal tests, ultrasounds, and joint mobility checks. Sanctuary officials emphasize that regular health monitoring allows them to detect diseases early, evaluate bone and muscle health, and provide these elderly animals with a safe, high-quality environment for the rest of their lives. Difficult words: infant (a very young child or baby animal), roam (to walk or move around freely without a specific plan or direction), comprehensive (including everything or dealing with all parts of something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Rescued chimpanzees from research laboratories now live safely at a sanctuary in Liberia. Many were taken from the wild as babies and lived in laboratories for many years. Today, they live together in groups on islands where they can move around freely. These West African chimpanzees are critically endangered because their population is dropping quickly. Specialists at the sanctuary give the animals full health checks to care for them as they get older. Doctors check their blood, bones, and muscles, and do ultrasounds to make sure they are healthy. Regular checks help the team find sickness early and give the chimpanzees good care for the rest of their lives. Difficult words: sanctuary (a safe place where animals or people are protected from harm), endangered (in danger), ultrasound (a medical test to see pictures of the inside of the body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Rescued chimpanzees from laboratories now live in a safe place in Liberia. They live on big islands where they can walk around freely. Long ago, people take them from the forest as small babies. Then they spend years in laboratories. Today, there are only a few chimpanzees in the wild. Doctors give them full health checks to keep them safe as they grow old. They test their blood, check their bones, and look for sickness early. Health checks give these rescued animals a safe and happy life. Difficult words: rescued (when someone saves you from a bad situation), laboratory (a room where scientists do experiments and tests), sickness (the state when your body does not feel well). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

India has built a multi-billion-dollar medical tourism industry that attracts hundreds of thousands of international patients every year, mainly from South Asia, the Middle East, and Africa. Patients choose India because of its highly skilled English-speaking doctors, accredited private hospitals, shorter waiting times, and low treatment costs. For example, complex surgeries in India can cost up to ten times less than in the US. Furthermore, international patients pay in cash, which provides hospitals with funds to invest in advanced technology. However, India’s top position is facing serious challenges. Geopolitical conflicts interrupt international travel, while strong competitors like Thailand, Turkey, and South Korea are aggressively marketing their specialized procedures. To maintain its global position, India is shifting its focus toward innovation. Health tech startups in Bangalore are developing advanced AI devices for early cancer detection and brain mapping. Experts believe India must now transform its brand from merely cheap care to a world leader in quality, technology, and trust. Difficult words: accredited (officially approved and certified by an organization for meeting high standards), fund (an amount of money saved or made available for a particular purpose ), merely (nothing more than what you say). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

India is a major global center for medical tourism. Every year, many foreign patients travel there for complex surgeries and medical care. India offers very low prices, excellent private hospitals, and highly trained doctors. Patients also like that they don’t have to wait long to see a specialist . Most foreign patients come from nearby countries like Bangladesh, as well as parts of Africa and the Middle East. But other countries like Turkey, Thailand, and South Korea are becoming very popular too. To stay competitive , India is investing in new technology and AI. Startups are building smart devices to detect diseases earlier and plan difficult operations. Today, India wants to show the world that it offers high-quality and modern technology, not just low prices. Difficult words: complex (difficult to understand or do), specialist (a person who is an expert in a specific area), competitive (as good as or better than others of a similar type). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

India is a famous place for medical tourism . Many sick people travel to India every year. The country has very good private hospitals and clever doctors. The treatments are much cheaper than in Western countries. Patients do not wait long for operations. Many patients come from Africa and Asia. Today, other countries like Thailand and Turkey also want more patients from different countries. To stay ahead, Indian companies are using new technology and AI to help doctors. India wants to show that its healthcare is modern, safe, and high quality, not only cheap. Difficult words: medical tourism (when people travel to another country to undergo operations), private (a business that a person or business runs, not a government), treatment (medical care which a patient gets). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The UN General Assembly voted to replace the traditional Mercator world map with the Equal Earth map to show Africa’s true size. Proposed by Togo and supported by 164 nations, the non-binding resolution aims to influence education and governments worldwide. Critics argue the Mercator map distorts landmasses by making equatorial regions, such as Africa, look much smaller than countries near the poles, like Greenland or Alaska. Cartographer Clancy Wilmott explains that neither map is real; the Mercator projection was created for navigation, while equal-area projections accurately maintain geographic proportions. The United States was the only nation to vote against the resolution and claimed it is part of an ideological movement. However, experts view this change as a practical step toward better representing global issues like aid, health, and development. Difficult words: non-binding (an official decision or rule that people do not legally have to follow), distort (to change the shape, appearance, or meaning of something so that it is not natural or true), cartographer (a person who designs and draws maps). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The UN voted to change the traditional world map to a new one called the Equal Earth map. This new map shows the real size of Africa and countries near the equator . The old Mercator map was made for ocean travel, so it makes places near the poles, like Greenland, look much bigger than they really are. Most countries supported the non-binding resolution , but the United States voted against it. They called the idea political. Experts say that no flat map is perfect, but the new map helps people see the true size of continents. This change will help schools and governments understand world issues much better. Difficult words: equator (an imaginary line around the middle of the Earth that divides it into the Northern and Southern halves), non-binding (an official decision or rule that people do not legally have to follow), resolution (a formal decision or statement agreed on by a group or organization after a vote). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The UN vote for a new world map. The old map makes Africa look very small, and Greenland look very big. The new map shows the true size of all continents and countries. Most countries like the new map, but the USA vote no. The USA says that this idea is only about politics. Map experts say that the old map is good for ships. But the new map is better for schools and learning. It helps people see the world correctly . People will better understand some problems in the world. Difficult words: true (real), vote (to officially say yes or no to something or someone), correctly (without mistakes). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Argentine football legend Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football at the age of 39. In an emotional statement on Instagram, Messi shared that although the decision hurts deeply, the time has come to step away and make room for younger players. His decision comes shortly after playing in his sixth World Cup and following the recent passing of his father. Messi leaves behind an extraordinary international legacy as Argentina’s all-time leading goalscorer with 125 goals in 207 appearances. During his 20-year career with the national team, he won two Copa América titles and captained Argentina to World Cup victory in Qatar in 2022. While Messi has retired from international duty, he continues to play club football for Inter Miami in the United States. Fans and sports commentators around the world are calling his announcement the end of an historic era in modern football. Difficult words: legacy (something valuable or important that a person leaves behind after they finish their career or life), captain (to lead a sports team or group as its captain). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Famous football player Lionel Messi decided to stop playing for the Argentina national team. The 39-year-old superstar said on Instagram that it was a difficult decision , but it was the right time. He played for Argentina for 20 years, scored 125 goals, and played in 207 games. His biggest success was winning the World Cup in 2022 in Qatar. He also won two Copa América titles. Messi said he gave everything to his team, but now young players need a chance. Messi will continue playing for his club, Inter Miami in the USA, but his international career is now over. Difficult words: decision (a choice that you make after thinking about different options), success (achieving a good result or reaching a goal you worked hard for). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Lionel Messi is stopping his work for the Argentina football team. He is 39 years old. Messi plays for Argentina for 20 years. He scores 125 goals. He wins the World Cup with Argentina in 2022. Messi says that he gives everything to his national team. But now it is time to stop. He wants young players to play now. People are sad, but they thank him for his great games. Messi will continue playing for his club team. His team is Inter Miami in the USA. Difficult words: national (about a whole country), continue (to keep doing something, not to stop). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A major flash flood struck the Grand Canyon in Arizona. It left at least two people dead, several missing, and dozens needed to be evacuated by helicopter. The severe flooding occurred in Bright Angel Canyon, where Bright Angel Creek transformed into a dangerous torrent . According to experts, flash floods happen regularly during the southwest monsoon season, but fatalities are rare. The intensity of this particular flood was greatly increased by a recent wildfire, which destroyed vegetation and left bare soil unable to absorb rain. As a result, massive amounts of mud, rocks, and debris washed down into the canyon and destroyed the Trans Canyon Pipeline that supplies fresh water to the South Rim. Experts emphasize that hikers in remote areas must check weather forecasts and head to high ground immediately when severe storms threaten the region. Difficult words: torrent (a fast, strong, and dangerous stream of water), monsoon (a season of heavy rain and strong winds in certain parts of the world), fatality (a death caused by an accident, war, or natural disaster). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A big flash flood hit the Grand Canyon in Arizona after heavy rain. At least two people died, and helicopters had to rescue many visitors. Experts say that floods happen every year during the summer monsoon season. But this flood was much worse because a recent wildfire burned many trees on the hills. Without trees, the heavy rain quickly pushed mud, rocks, and wood down into the canyon. The fast water also destroyed an important pipeline that gives fresh water to hotels and visitors. Weather experts warn that storms can start very quickly in the canyon. Because there is often no phone service, hikers must check the weather before walking in dangerous areas and always move to high ground during heavy rain. Difficult words: monsoon (a season of heavy rain in some parts of the world), pipeline (a long pipe used to carry water, oil, or gas), hiker (a person who walks in the countryside or mountains for fun). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a big flood in the Grand Canyon. A lot of rain falls very fast. Two people die. Helicopters help many visitors to safety . In summer, it rains a lot in this area. A recent forest fire makes the flood worse. There are no trees to hold the water. The dirty water takes rocks and mud down the hills. The flood also breaks a big water pipe. Weather experts say that people must be careful. When it rains in the canyon, hikers must run up to high ground to stay safe. Difficult words: safety (a place where nothing bad can happen to you), recent (something what happens a short time ago), hiker (a person who walks in the countryside or mountains for fun). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

News in Levels helps students learn English. Do you know how to use News in Levels correctly? This little manual can help you. Read two articles every day. It is important to do something for your English every day. Listen to last 10 articles. When you walk or travel to somewhere, try to say aloud to yourself what were the articles about. It is important to do these three activities every day, ideally 30 minutes reading, 30 minutes listening and 30 minutes speaking. If you like News in Levels, please send this link to your friends who could also benefit from this website – www.newsinlevels.com . Thank you very much. Have a nice day, News in Levels team

Icelanders have voted against resuming membership talks with the EU in a national referendum. With almost all votes counted, 52.5% of voters rejected the government’s proposal to restart negotiations, while 47.5% supported it. Prime Minister’s government had brought the vote forward due to global geopolitical tensions; however, international issues didn’t dominate the debate . Political experts explained that the NO campaign successfully focused on domestic identity, national independence, and protecting Iceland’s fishing waters. In contrast, the YES campaign ran a very technical campaign that failed to excite the public. Even though the referendum was only about reopening preliminary discussions rather than deciding on actual EU membership, voters chose to protect their sovereignty . This result stops Iceland’s path toward joining the EU for the near future. Difficult words: dominate (to be the strongest, most important, or most noticeable part of something), debate (a formal discussion on a topic where people express different opinions), sovereignty (the power and right of a country to govern itself without control from outside). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People in Iceland voted No in a referendum about the EU. They decided not to restart talks about joining the EU. About 52.5% of people voted No, and 47.5% voted Yes. The Prime Minister wanted to hold the vote earlier because of global problems, but the political debate stayed focused on local issues. Many Icelanders wanted to protect their national independence and their fishing waters. Political experts said that the NO group made a strong campaign about identity and feelings. The YES group only talked about technical details, so they couldn’t convince enough people. As a result, Iceland will remain outside the European Union. Difficult words: debate (a formal discussion), independence (when a country is free and is not controlled by another country), identity (the qualities, beliefs, and culture that make a person or a country who or what they are). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Iceland has a big vote about the European Union. Most people vote No. They do not want to talk about joining the EU. About 52.5% vote No and 47.5% voted Yes. Icelanders want to stay independent . They also want to protect their fish and waters. Fewer people say Yes because the NO group does not have interesting ideas. The government wants to start new talks, but the people say no. Iceland will not join the European Union now. Difficult words: join (to become part of a group or organization), independent (when a country is free, without control of another country), government (people who officially rule and control a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Australia, high property prices and rising cost-of-living pressures are forcing more families to live together under one roof. Many young adults are postponing or completely abandoning their plans to buy their first homes. As a result, the number of multigenerational households grew by 22% between 2016 and 2021, and experts expect this trend to accelerate. To cope with these financial challenges, older generations are adapting their homes. Some grandparents are renovating their houses to accommodate adult grandchildren, while others are buying modular homes to place on their children’s land. Many families find positive benefits in this arrangement, such as shared living costs and built-in help with childcare. In response to this demand, secondary dwellings such as granny flats are becoming increasingly popular. Industry leaders are now calling for simpler planning laws to make it easier to build these small homes across the country. Difficult words: abandon (to give up on something completely or leave it behind), multigenerational (involving several generations of a family living or working together), dwelling (a house, apartment, or other place where people live). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Houses are very expensive in Australia, so many young people cannot buy their first home. Because of high living costs, more generations are deciding to live together in one house. Between 2016 and 2021, the number of families living this way increased by 22%. Grandparents are helping by rebuilding their homes or adding small houses in their backyards . This arrangement brings many benefits . Families save money, and parents get extra help with child care. To help more people, industry experts want the government to change building rules. They want it to be easier for families to build small extra houses, called granny flats, in their backyards. Difficult words: backyard (an open area behind a house, usually covered with grass or a garden), arrangement (a plan between people about how something will work or be), benefit (a good or helpful result of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Houses in Australia are very expensive today. Young people cannot buy their own homes. Because of this, many families live together in one big house. Grandparents, parents, and adult children share space to save money. Some older people build small homes in their children’s gardens. Living together helps everyone. Grandparents help with children, and young people get a cheap place to live. The number of families living together is growing fast every year. Between 2016 and 2021, it goes up by 22%. Difficult words: expensive (when something costs a lot of money), adult (a person who is not a child anymore), cheap (when something costs little money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

More people live alone, and many adults don’t have a partner. In the United States, half of young men and women don’t live with a partner, and similar changes happen in other countries. The rise of single life grows because people have stopped dating for some time, for example, during the pandemic. Younger adults don’t learn basic skills to meet people or manage feelings of rejection . Technology also changes dating. Many people meet online and can choose partners using rules about height, job, or education. Some choices reduce the number of possible partners. Also, women have more freedom and education, and want men with good jobs and respect. Many single people enjoy their life and freedom, but 60 to 70 per cent want to have a partner. Some people feel lonely or sad because they can’t meet the right person. Social problems also happen when single people grow, for example, the need for smaller houses and a falling number of children. Even in countries where men and women are equal , the number of single people continues to grow. Difficult words: rejection (when someone says “no” to you or doesn’t accept you), freedom (the ability to choose what you want or do what you like), equal (when people have the same rights). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

More adults live alone and don’t have a partner. In the United States, about half of young men and women don’t have a partner. The number of single people grows because some adults stop dating for some time, like during the pandemic. People miss learning how to meet someone and handle rejection . Phones and online apps also change dating. People can choose partners with rules about jobs, education, or height. These rules make it harder to find a partner. Women often want men with good jobs and respect. Many single people like being alone, but most want a partner. Some people feel sad or lonely when they cannot meet the right person. This change also affects society , for example, people want smaller houses, and there are fewer babies. Experts don’t know when this will stop. Difficult words: dating (spending time with someone you like to be your partner), rejection (when someone says no to you), society (a large group of people living together in a place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many people live alone. Some adults do not have a partner. In the United States, about half of young men and women do not have a partner. The pandemic makes dating difficult. People do not know how to meet someone or what to do when someone says “no.” Phones and online apps change how people meet. People can choose partners with rules about work, school, or height . These rules make it harder to find a partner. Some people like being alone, but many want a partner. Some people feel sad or lonely when they cannot meet the right person. This change also changes life. People need more small houses and have fewer children. Experts do not know when this will stop. Difficult words: adult (a person who is not a child anymore), dating (spending time with someone you like to be your partner), height (how tall a person is). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Norway is mourning the death of King Harald V, who passed away at the age of 89 after a 35-year reign. He was Europe’s oldest monarch and became widely loved for modernizing the monarchy. Over the decades, he broke traditions by marrying a commoner , Queen Sonja, and by serving as a compassionate voice of national unity. King Harald supported minorities, migrants, and the LGBTQ+ community, and was famous for his inclusive speeches emphasizing that all people belong to modern Norway. He also provided comfort to the nation during tragedies, such as the 2011 terror attacks. Following his passing, his son succeeded to the throne as King Haakon VIII without a coronation ceremony. Despite recent scandals within the royal family and growing public debate surrounding the institution, Norwegians remember King Harald V as an empathetic, grandfatherly figure who successfully adapted the monarchy to a modern democratic society. Difficult words: commoner (a person who is not a member of the royal family), compassionate (feeling or showing sympathy, care, and concern for others who are suffering), coronation (a ceremony at which a person is formally made a king or queen). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Norwegians are sad because King Harald V died at the age of 89. He was the king of Norway for 35 years and was very popular. People loved him because he was kind, warm, and brought the country together. He welcomed immigrants and supported the LGBTQ+ community. After his death, his son became the new King Haakon VIII. The new king promised to serve his country using his father’s motto : Everything for Norway. Even though there were some recent scandals in the royal family, many people in Norway still love their monarchy . They will remember King Harald V as a caring leader and a grandfather figure for the whole nation. Difficult words: motto (a short sentence which expresses what a person thinks or believes), scandal (an action or event which causes public shock or anger because it is morally wrong), monarchy (a system in which there is a king or queen as the leader of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

King Harald V of Norway dies. He is 89 years old. He is king for 35 years. People in Norway are very sad. He is a good and kind king who helps everyone. He cares about immigrants and minorities . Many people say that he is like a grandfather to the country. Now, his son is the new King Haakon VIII. The new king says that he will work hard for Norway. Many people put flowers at the royal palace to remember the late king. Difficult words: immigrant (a person who comes to live in another country), minority (a smaller group of people who are somehow different from others), royal palace (the large building where a king or queen officially lives). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Construction worker Phineas Gage survived a terrible accident in 1848 when an iron rod shot through his skull, destroying a large section of his right frontal lobe , the part of the brain associated with behavior and emotion. Although he physically recovered, his personality drastically changed; the once reliable man became rude and capricious . Friends famously claimed, ‘’Gage was no longer Gage.’’ However, his case provided the first insights into the brain’s flexibility, a concept now known as neuroplasticity. Gage later moved to Chile and worked as a stagecoach driver, a job that required significant cognitive effort, including memorization and steering multiple horses. This regular, repetitive activity served as self-directed neurorehabilitation. His recovery demonstrated that the adult brain is not fixed and can adapt by reallocating functions, a process called cortical remapping. Gage’s survival and subsequent recovery changed the understanding of the brain, establishing him as a key figure in neuroscience and offering hope for recovery from brain injuries and mental health challenges today. Difficult words: lobe (a rounded, often curved section that is part of a larger organ), stagecoach (a large, enclosed four-wheeled vehicle pulled by horses that was historically used to carry passengers and mail over long distances), subsequent (coming after something else in time or order). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 1848, construction worker Phineas Gage survived a bad accident when an iron rod destroyed the front part of his brain. While he didn’t die, his personality changed completely; the organized man became rude and unreliable . This case was very important because it showed that the brain and personality are connected to specific areas. Gage later found work driving a stagecoach in Chile. This difficult, repetitive job was like therapy, forcing his brain to adapt and change itself. Gage’s recovery showed doctors that the brain is flexible, and his survival started the field of neuroscience. We now know that the brain can adapt and recover from serious injuries, which gives hope to patients today. Difficult words: rod (a thin, straight, solid bar), unreliable (not able to be trusted or counted on), stagecoach (a large vehicle pulled by horses that carried people and mail on a fixed route a long time ago), repetitive (a task or job which you do over and over again), survival (staying alive after an accident). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 1848, construction worker Phineas Gage has a bad accident. An iron rod goes through his head and hurts the front part of his brain . Gage does not die, but his personality changes. He is not kind and organized anymore. This event is important for doctors. It shows that the brain and personality are connected to some parts of the brain. Gage later finds work in Chile. His job is repetitive . For Gage, it is a therapy. His brain must learn to work differently. Doctors learn that the brain can change. Gage’s accident starts a new field of neuroscience. It teaches us that the brain can adapt and recover from serious injuries. Difficult words: rod (a thin, straight, solid bar), brain (the organ inside the head), personality (how you act and what you think), repetitive (when something happens again and again). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Meta has agreed to pay an 18 billion-dollar (16.5 billion euros) settlement to resolve claims from 48 US states, Washington, D.C., and three territories. The legal actions accused Facebook and Instagram of harming children’s mental health through addictive features. Although Meta denied any wrongdoing, the company agreed to pay the sum in annual instalments over a 10-year period to avoid potentially higher fines. Beyond the financial settlement, Meta will introduce significant online safety features for teenage users. These include a default two-hour daily time limit, automatic night-time blocks between midnight and 6:00 AM, and restrictions during school hours. Additionally, Meta plans to hide like counts and photo filters that simulate cosmetic surgery. However, Meta insists that 30% of the funds will only be released if competitors like TikTok and YouTube adopt similar safety restrictions, which started a debate about industry-wide accountability . Difficult words: installment (one of several regular payments made over time to pay for something), default (a setting or option that is automatically chosen by a system if you don’t change it yourself), accountability (responsibility for your actions and ability to explain them when something goes wrong). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The company Meta agreed to pay a big settlement of 18 billion dollars (16.5 billion euros) to 48 American states. US officials accused Facebook and Instagram of harming the health of children. Meta said it didn’t do anything wrong, but the company agreed to pay the money over ten years. Meta will also add new safety rules for teenagers on Facebook and Instagram. Teenagers will have a two-hour daily time limit, and the apps will be blocked at night and during school hours. Meta will also hide the number of likes on posts to help young people feel better. Meta wants other big companies, like TikTok and YouTube, to follow these new safety rules as well to make the internet safer for all children. Difficult words: settlement (an official agreement that resolves a disagreement or court case, often involving money), accuse (to say that someone has done something wrong, dishonest, or illegal), hide (to put something where people cannot see it, to not show something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The company Meta must pay 18 billion dollars (16.5 billion euros) to 48 US states. US leaders say Facebook and Instagram are bad for children’s health . Meta says that it does nothing wrong, but it will pay the money over ten years. Meta is also changing how teenagers use its apps. Teenagers will only use the apps for two hours a day. The apps will stop working at night and during school time. Meta also wants to hide the number of likes. Meta wants other video apps like TikTok and YouTube to make the same changes for children, too. People are asking how safe these apps are for children. Difficult words: health (how your body and mind are), hide (not to show something), change (when something becomes different). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

US President Donald Trump issued an executive order renaming Lake Ontario as Lake America , which escalated tensions amid ongoing US-Canada trade disputes. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney quickly dismissed the move and stated that the body of water remains Lake Ontario. An international affairs expert described the symbolic name change as an attempt to project power and insult foreign leaders. Most Canadians view the action with mild amusement rather than anger, and say it is childish provocation. The incident highlights growing international concerns about the American president’s erratic judgment and style of governance. Trump is facing economic challenges at home, including inflation, high national debt, and low approval ratings ahead of upcoming midterm elections, and he appears to be using anti-Canadian rhetoric to get domestic political support. Analysts point out that US voters and key trading states remain skeptical, and they recognize Canada as an essential economic partner and long-standing historical ally. Difficult words: insult (to say or do something that causes someone to feel hurt or disrespected), amusement (the feeling of being entertained or finding something funny), provocation (an action intended to make someone angry, annoyed, or react strongly), erratic (changing unpredictably or acting in a strange, inconsistent way). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

US President Donald Trump signed an order to change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America . This decision happened during a difficult trade war between the United States and Canada. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney responded calmly and said that the lake will always keep its original name. Most Canadians are not angry, but they see this move as a silly political game. Trump is currently facing many big problems at home, including a weak economy, high prices, and upcoming political elections. Experts believe he is picking fights with neighboring countries to get attention and support from American voters. But many Americans still view Canada as a close friend and important business partner, which makes Trump’s actions unpopular on both sides of the border. Difficult words: trade war (a fight where countries hurt each other’s business), upcoming (when something happens or arrives soon in the near future ), attention (notice, interest, or thought given to someone or something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Donald Trump wants to change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America . This decision makes many people in Canada laugh. Canada’s Prime Minister says that the lake will always be Lake Ontario. Experts say that Trump is doing this because he is having trade problems with Canada. Trump also has economic problems in the United States. He wants more votes in the next election . Most people in Canada and America do not like this name change. They know that both countries need to be good friends and do business together. Difficult words: decision (what you want to do after careful thinking), trade (buying and selling things and services), election (a formal process of voting to choose a person for a job in politics). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Austria, the construction of a new business park on the grounds of a former Nazi concentration camp has sparked widespread outrage. The historic Hirtenberg site, a subcamp of Mauthausen, held around 400 female prisoners during World War II who were forced into slave labor. Despite archaeological evidence confirming the location’s historical significance , Austria’s Federal Monuments Office decided the surviving physical remains were insufficient for official protection. Consequently, developers have begun building warehouse facilities and a supermarket on the property. Activists, historians, and memorial organizations strongly oppose the project and say that sacred history is being sacrificed for economic interests. They emphasize that physical evidence of Nazi atrocities must be preserved rather than replaced by modern commercial structures. Although the local developer has offered to fund a memorial, critics say that building over a former concentration camp disrespects the victims and undermines historic memory in a nation that historically struggled to confront its Nazi past. Difficult words: significance (being important, meaningful, or having a great effect), sacrifice (to give up something valuable or important for a specific purpose or cause), atrocity (an extremely cruel, violent, or shocking act committed against people). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A new project in Austria is causing anger because workers are building a business park on the site of a former Nazi camp. During World War II, about 400 women were kept at the Hirtenberg camp and forced to work in a factory. Today, developers are building a supermarket and large storage buildings on this land. Officials said there were not enough old buildings left to legally protect the site, but historians and activists feel sad and angry. They believe that places with dark history should be saved, not used for shopping and business. The company building the park offered to pay for a small memorial . Even so, many people think that building over a concentration camp forgets the victims and hides important history. Difficult words: historian (a person who studies, researches, and writes about the past), memorial (an object, structure, or event created to remember a person or important event), victim (a person who is harmed or killed as a result of a crime, accident, or war). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The fashion industry relies heavily on toxic petrochemical dyes that pollute oceans and damage ecosystems. To solve this environmental crisis, the biotechnology company Colorifix has developed a sustainable way to produce dyes using nature instead of harmful chemistry. By inserting natural genetic code into bacteria, the company ferments pigment in tanks through a process similar to brewing beer. The biological dye and biomass replace synthetic chemicals, which significantly reduces environmental impact. On polycotton fabrics, this method saves up to 77 percent of water, 51 percent of energy, and 31 percent of carbon emissions. The company tests all dyes for safety to make sure they don’t cause skin irritation or allergies. Their products are durable against sunlight and washing, which makes them attractive to major fashion brands. It now ships ready-to-use dye concentrates globally and proves that high-performance textile colors can be produced cleanly without depending on fossil fuels. Difficult words: petrochemical (a chemical substance made from oil or natural gas), ferment (to change a substance using natural microorganisms like bacteria or yeast), polycotton (a blended fabric made from a mix of polyester and natural cotton). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On some fabrics, it saves up to 77 percent of water and reduces carbon emissions. The company tests every new color carefully to make sure it is safe for human skin and doesn’t fade in sunlight or washing. Big fashion brands are now starting to use these new biological dyes. The company’s boss believes we should stop using harmful chemicals for clothes because nature can make every color safely. Difficult words: dye (a substance used to change the colour of clothes, hair, or other materials), brew (to make a liquid drink by mixing ingredients and letting them sit in liquid, fade (to slowly lose brightness, strength, or colour over time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Arkestra dance shows take place in rural parts of India and attract large groups of men to night events. Young women dance on stage for many hours, often under strong pressure from the crowd. The shows bring money and excitement to fairs and villages; however, they also create danger for the women who perform. Many dancers enter this work because of poverty and a lack of other jobs. Some start when they are still very young, and middlemen often bring them into the shows. On stage, women face harassment , touching, and threats. Off stage, they face shame from family and society, which can hurt their future. Police and social workers say some girls are forced into this work through illegal networks. Police sometimes rescue very young girls, but many later return because their families need money. The shows continue because men pay to watch, and deep social rules make change slow. Difficult words: pressure (strong force that makes someone feel they must do something), poverty (having very little money), middleman (a person who brings workers and customers together and takes money), harassment (bad or rude actions that make someone feel unsafe or uncomfortable). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: exciting (when something makes you feel happy, interested, or full of energy), continue (to still happen), return (to go back to a place or situation).

Taylor Swift is not just a famous singer; she also brings a lot of money to cities. Her tours, albums, and merchandise make fans spend on tickets, travel, and hotels. Experts call this effect ‘Swiftenomics’ and study how her popularity shows her power in business. She can charge high prices for tickets because many people want to see her live, but seats are limited. Taylor’s success comes from her authenticity and connection with fans. She writes about her real experiences, breaks some rules, and inspires many women. Misty Heggeness wrote about Taylor Swift’s economic influence. According to her, Swift teaches lessons about leading, creating, and not giving up. Taylor changes herself and uses smart ways to sell albums, like offering many versions to meet high demand . She also tells stories about historical women in her songs and rewrites them from a woman’s point of view. This shows fans how women can be strong, smart, and successful. Her example challenges old ideas that often left out women’s work. Difficult words: merchandise (things a singer or company sells, like T-shirts, posters, or albums), authenticity (being real, true, and not fake), demand (how much people want something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Five teenage boys died in County Kildare, Ireland, after driving a stolen BMW the wrong way down a highway and colliding head-on with another car. The victims in the second vehicle, a family traveling to the airport, suffered severe injuries, and two adults remain in critical condition. Accounts belonging to some of the deceased boys contained videos showing stolen cars, reckless driving, and escaping police pursuits . Following the horrific incident, Ireland’s media regulator contacted TikTok to investigate its efforts in removing dangerous joyriding content. Irish Prime Minister condemned the behavior and stated that reckless driving is increasingly staged to gain popularity and likes on social media platforms. Police representatives warned that rival youth gangs actively try to outdo each other online through dangerous driving stunts. In response, TikTok stated that it is closely monitoring related content and continuously removing accounts that violate safety rules regarding criminal behavior. Difficult words: deceased (dead), pursuit (chasing or following someone quickly to catch them), joyriding (stealing a car and driving it fast and dangerously for fun). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Reports revealed that the boys had previously posted videos on social media which showed stolen cars and dangerous driving to get likes and followers on social media. The Irish government and police blamed social media platforms for encouraging this reckless behavior. Officials are now contacting TikTok to ensure the company takes down these dangerous videos. TikTok claimed it is actively monitoring the platform and deleting accounts that break its rules against illegal actions. Difficult words: highway (a fast road which connects cities), blame (to say or think that someone or something is responsible for a bad event or mistake), reckless (doing something dangerous without caring about the risks or safety of others). People sleep in many positions, but experts usually talk about three main ones: side, back, or stomach. Sleep habits feel personal; however, the way people sleep can affect their bodies and health. In the past, some experts believed sleep position showed personality, but there is no strong proof for this idea. Still, research shows that sleep position can have an impact on pain, breathing, and comfort. Each position has good and bad sides. Sleeping on the stomach is the least common and often not advised, because it can hurt the spine and neck. Sleeping on the back can help people with lower back pain, especially with a pillow under the knees. However, this position can cause snoring and breathing problems for some people. Many experts suggest sleeping on the side. This position can help keep the spine in line and reduce problems like heartburn . The left or right side may matter for some health problems. There is no perfect choice for everyone, and moving during sleep is normal and helpful. Difficult words: spine (bones of the back), snore (to make loud breathing sounds while sleeping), heartburn (a hot or burning feeling in the chest or throat). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People sleep in different ways, but experts say that people mostly sleep on their side, back, or stomach. Sleep position feels personal, but it can have an impact on health. Some old ideas link sleep position to personality , but experts don’t believe this. Modern research shows that sleep position can change how the body feels in the morning. Sleeping on the stomach is not popular and often causes neck or back pain. Sleeping on the back can help with lower back pain, but it can also cause snoring and breathing trouble. For this reason, some people shouldn’t sleep on their backs. Many doctors recommend sleeping on the side. It helps the back stay straight and can reduce heartburn . The left or right side may help with different health problems. People move a lot during sleep, and this movement helps the body feel better. Difficult words: personality (the way a person thinks, feels, and acts), snore (to make loud breathing sounds while sleeping), heartburn (a hot or burning feeling in the chest or throat). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: stomach (the body part where food goes after you eat), impact (a strong effect or change), comfortable (relaxed and without bad feelings).
